Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; David Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Underwriting Officer; Johnathan Hargrove, Chief Investment Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; and Emily Vargas, Chief Claims Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Reynolds.

Michael Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q3 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by robust new business production, disciplined underwriting reflected in our combined ratio improvements, manageable catastrophe losses, solid investment income yields, favorable realized gains alongside contained unrealized losses, a diversified asset allocation, and a fortified capital position. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation initiatives.

David, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

David Thompson: Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $1.85 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included strong new business growth, catastrophe management, combined ratio discipline, investment yields, gains realization, asset diversification, and capital strength. Our combined ratio was 93.2%. Investment income for the quarter was $1.45 billion. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with RBC at 462%. Our expense ratio also improved to 26.8%.

Let me expand on these areas starting with catastrophe losses, which are always a focal point for P&C carriers like us amid rising climate volatility. Catastrophe losses—or cats—include pre-tax losses net of reinsurance from major events like named storms, wildfires, floods, and severe storms above our $10 million retention per event. We track this in dollars and as a percentage of gross written premium, or GWP, to show the earnings impact relative to top-line growth.

In Q3 2024, cats totaled $452 million, or 4.2% of our $10.8 billion GWP. This was down from Q2's $520 million or 4.8% of GWP, but up slightly from Q3 2023's $410 million or 3.9%. Through nine months, we're at $1.42 billion, or 4.1% of year-to-date GWP, within our full-year guidance of 3.5% to 4.5%. This outperforms industry averages; for instance, global insured cat losses were about 5.2% of premiums in 2023 per Swiss Re, and peers like Chubb and Travelers expect 4-6% this year due to secondary perils.

By event, peak winds from Hurricane Beryl in Texas and the Carolinas made up 55% or $249 million, thunderstorms added 25% or $113 million, California wildfires $65 million, and European floods $25 million. Secondary perils now at 42% of cats, up from 32% in 2022, tied to climate shifts like La Niña and Arctic amplification. North America took 72% or $325 million, hitting U.S. personal property hardest with combined ratios at 112% in Florida and Texas. Europe was 12% with tight exposure limits post-2021 floods, Asia-Pacific 10% from Typhoon Gaemi impacting agribusiness. Reinsurance recoveries were solid at 68% ceded or $307 million, with attachments up 15% year-over-year to $150 million via Swiss Re and RenaissanceRe.

Trends show cat frequency up 8% year-over-year per RMS v18 models, severity up 12% from rebuilding costs now +25% per CoreLogic. Our loss-adjusted premiums rose 9.2% globally, stabilizing the cat load. Five-year average cat loss ratio is 3.8%, below the 10-year peak of 5.2%. We've invested $45 million in cat modeling with AIR Worldwide's Touchstone and our Exposure360 AI tool, boosting PML accuracy 22% and exiting 15% of high-risk Florida cat bond tranches. Reinsurance includes new ILWs and parametric triggers for wildfires and floods, booking $250 million GWP from California clients. U.S. commercial property rates up 11.5%, cat layers 18%, aligning with Allianz and Munich Re.

For full-year 2024, we guide $1.9-2.1 billion or 3.8-4.2% of $50 billion GWP, assuming NOAA's normalized Atlantic outlook. Q4 risks like Santa Ana winds are hedged with 75% quota share on West Coast risks. Long-term, targeting sub-3.5% cat load by 2026 via EMEA/APAC growth to 35% of book and drone telematics.

Next, new business production volume, a leading indicator of growth and value. We achieved $2.8 billion in annualized premium equivalent, or APE, up 18% year-over-year from $2.37 billion and 7% sequentially from Q1's $2.62 billion. Policy count hit 1.45 million new policies, up 22% from 1.19 million, our ninth straight double-digit APE quarter, beating AM Best's 12% industry average. PVNBP was $5.4 billion for multi-year durability, NBV $420 million up 25% with margins at 15.5% from pricing and lower costs.

By segment: P&C at 62% or $1.74 billion, up 21%, with commercial 28% growth including $450 million E&S and parametric products 15%. Personal auto/homeowners added 850,000 policies up 16% via AetherDrive telematics, cutting loss ratios 2.5 points. Life & Health 28% or $784 million up 14%, group health $320 million up 19%, individual life $280 million led by IUL. Specialty 10% or $276 million up 15%, cyber $120 million up 35% with D&O extensions.

Regions: North America 55% or $1.54 billion up 24% with 820,000 policies, U.S. E&S share at 4.2% per Verisk. Europe 25% or $700 million up 12%, Asia-Pacific 15% or $420 million up 22% via India micro-insurance and Australia cyber. Rest 5% up 16%.

Digital channels 42% of new business with 28% conversion via AetherNow API, STP at 65% cutting costs 18% to $210 per policy. 60% high-NBV products. Q3 guide $2.9-3.1 billion APE, 17-20% growth.

Turning to combined ratio, our profitability benchmark. Overall accident year at 93.2%, 310 basis points better than Q2 2023's 96.3% and 50 basis points ahead of Q1's 93.7%. Ex-cats of $245 million or 4.2 points, adjusted at 89.0%, best non-cat since Q3 2019. Year-to-date 93.8%, on track for 92-94% full-year. Favorable prior development 1.8 points from auto physical damage.

Loss ratio 66.4% down 220 basis points on 8.2% earned rate vs. 5-6% auto/7% property trends, moderating social inflation. Expense ratio 26.8% down 90 basis points from tech efficiencies, STP at 92% for auto.

Personal Lines 52% premiums $2.8 billion, 90.5%: Auto 89.2% with 68% telematics pricing high-risk 15% better; homeowners 93.1% with 2.1 cat points, non-cat 91.0%, non-renewed 12% Florida. Premiums up 11% to $5.6 billion annualized.

Commercial 38% $2.1 billion, 95.1% improved 420 basis points: Workers' comp 93.8% with 2.5 development, AI triage cutting LAE 8%; auto/liability 96.5% non-cat 93.3%; property 94.2% rates up 10.5%. Premiums up 9% to $4.2 billion.

Specialty/reinsurance 10% $550 million, 96.8%: E&S Gulf Coast managed via 40% quota share. U.S. 92.8%, Europe 95.2%, Asia 97.5%.

Initiatives: GenAI underwriting 65% small fleet, Guidewire cloud for $50 million savings; divested $300 million California property; reinsurance costs down 5%. Outlook 91-93% ex-cat.

On investments, net income $1.45 billion up 12%, book yield 4.2% up 25 basis points. Realized gains $210 million up from $85 million, from corporate bonds like JPMorgan/Apple and equity trims in Microsoft/dividend stocks. Unrealized losses $2.1 billion or -1.7% of portfolio, better than industry -3.2%, mostly fixed income on rate rises. U.S. 85% AUM pressured, Europe gains on sovereigns, EM flat with FX hedges.

Active management via Aladdin shifted $5.7 billion to shorter HY munis/privates for 50 basis points yield lift. Forward yield 4.4-4.6%, spread 185 basis points beating peers.

Yield specifically at 4.35% annualized up 45 basis points year-over-year, 12 sequentially, strongest since Q4 2021. Fixed income 78% at 4.65%, corporates 5.1%; new money 5.4% vs. book 4.1%. Duration 5.8 years. U.S. munis 3.8% after-tax, Europe 3.2%, Asia 5.2%. Equities/alts 4.8%, private credit 6.7%. LDI 85% liabilities, ESG overlay, NAIC 1-2 at 92%. Full-year 4.4-4.6%.

Capital: Statutory surplus $15.8 billion up 9% year-over-year, 4% sequentially from $1.2 billion earnings retention and $450 million unrealized gains. RBC 462% vs. peers Chubb 420%, Travelers 380%. P&C 485% surplus $9.2 billion; life/annuity 440% $4.5 billion; health/specialty 425% $2.1 billion. U.S. 10% growth, cedes $300 million Florida risk. Surplus CAGR 8.5% past three years. $500 million buyback, dividend up 7% to $0.85. 2025 growth 8-10%, PML covered.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, David. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our property and casualty lines. We are actively managing our exposure to secondary perils like wildfires and floods, and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including AI-enhanced modeling and parametric products that align with the cat management and new business momentum David outlined.

Johnathan Hargrove: Thank you. From an investment perspective, we have continued to focus on diversifying our portfolio and managing risk in the current market environment. We are seeing positive returns from our investments across fixed income, equities, and alternatives.

With $285 billion in general account assets up 4% year-over-year from life/annuity cash flows, our allocation supports ALM for RBC over 500% U.S. and Solvency II Europe, yield at 4.85% up 25 basis points.

Fixed income 72% or $205 billion returned 4.2% vs. Bloomberg Aggregate 1.8%, duration 6.2 years: 45% IG corporates 5.1% YTW, 25% Treasuries/MBS, 15% RMBS/CMBS, 98% BBB+. U.S. 65%, Europe 20% 3.8%, Asia 15%. Aladdin for scenarios, $2.5 billion new floaters.

Equities 16% or $46 billion returned 8.7%, beta 0.85: 40% S&P ETF mega-tech, healthcare; 70% U.S., 20% Europe, 10% EM.

Alternatives 12% or $34 billion at 7.2%: private credit $8 billion 8.5% via Ares/Owl Rock, infrastructure $7 billion 6.8%, PE vintage-diversified. North America 60%, Asia 20%, Europe 20% ESG. Palantir for diligence.

NAV per share up 5.2% YoY, Sharpe 1.45. Shorten duration to 5.8%, alts to 15%, ESG 35%. Hedged recession, CRE 4% cap. Forward yield 5.0%+.

Emily Vargas: I'd like to briefly address our claims performance. We've implemented several initiatives to streamline our claims process and improve customer satisfaction, including AI triage and straight-through processing that tie into our expense improvements. We are seeing positive results in terms of reduced claims processing times, down significantly in auto and property lines.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the catastrophe loss trends and how they factor into your full-year outlook?

Michael Reynolds: Good morning, John. As David detailed, our Q3 cats at 4.2% of GWP were managed well through reinsurance and modeling upgrades. We're sticking to full-year guidance, with hedges in place for Q4, positioning us for stable margins.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of higher interest rates on your investment portfolio and yields?

David Thompson: Good morning, Maria. The higher-for-longer environment boosted our yield to 4.35%, with realized gains harvested strategically. Unrealized losses are contained and AFS, and our ALM keeps us resilient as rates stabilize.

Operator: Our next question comes from Alex Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Patel: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes around climate risk disclosure on your underwriting strategy?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Alex. We're ahead with RMS and AIR integrations for climate scenarios, non-renewing high-risk exposures, and parametric innovations. This enhances our risk selection without derailing growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Wong with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Karen Wong: Thanks. On new business, how sustainable is the 18% growth, especially in cyber and parametric?

David Thompson: Karen, digital channels and partnerships are scaling efficiently, with high-NBV focus. Q3 guide holds, and we're gaining share in resilient lines like cyber at 3.8% U.S. market.

Operator: [Potentially more questions]

Michael Reynolds: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
